decision_classes.agent_decidable: Resolve reversible technical and presentation choices inside the accepted product and visual envelope; generate paths, hashes, receipts, ledgers, and routine writes without asking the user.
decision_classes.owner_required: Ask only for missing product meaning or scope, new mobile scope, materially different visual direction, irreversible or costly choices, and acceptance or correction of a finished visual result.
decision_classes.external_authority: Use an already-authorized repository route; hard-block only when a required permission or external state is genuinely unavailable.

user_role_policy: The user's initial brief and later corrections are the sole authority for desired product meaning; repository sources are current-state evidence, not a second product owner.
The user describes the desired product path once with the agent; the agent records and carries that durable intent baseline through the program.
The user reviews finished visuals and corrects material product or visual mistakes.
Never ask the user to calculate hashes, name technical artifact owners, edit JSON, operate the ledger, choose routine tools, or repeat ordinary write permission already granted by the task.
The agent records natural-language decisions as canonical receipts and owns routine program coordination.
owner_surface: Lead with the stage's declared owner surface; use finished visuals or one compact review board only for G3-G6.
Show material exceptions and at most three questions.
Keep raw JSON, inventories, hashes, permissions, and validator logs in linked evidence.
Accept unambiguous natural-language decisions; never require identifiers or magic syntax.
invariants: A component catalog never substitutes for the all-screen atlas.
Desired product semantics come from the initial user brief and later user corrections; current product sources constrain factual compatibility but cannot silently redefine intent.
Generated views and passing receipts are assembled by scripts, not hand-edited.
Agent self-acceptance is prohibited; machine review readiness and user acceptance are separate states.
Responsive Web is required; mobile-specific product scope requires explicit current user authorization.
Current-gate success alone never permits the adjacent stage.
Historical contract profiles are read-only and cannot close active gates.
Determinism, source fidelity, native-image comparison, and visual-language conformance are separate claims.
The accepted pilot is normative for every applicable reusable UI clause; novel target semantics, content, data, actions, and screen-specific composition remain target-owned.
Applicability is independently derived and every clause application exact-covers conforms, accepted_exception, or source_backed_not_applicable; candidate-to-self comparison is never standard proof.

state_policy.review_ready: Machine evidence is complete and the finished result may be shown to the user; the stage remains non-terminal until the user accepts or requests a bounded revision.
state_policy.needs_input: Ledger-only non-terminal state for a material product question or finished-result review; resume the same row from typed owner-response evidence.
state_policy.blocked: Terminal only for authority, safety, evidence, permission, inseparable foreign change, or unavailable external state.
state_policy.revision: Create a replacement only when target, scope, dependencies, accepted sources, prompt requirements, or acceptance criteria materially change.

stage.title: Complete all-screen atlas
stage.objective: Represent every authoritative screen, state surface, overlay, shell, internal surface, and exclusion exactly once.
allowed_unresolved: G2 graph, family, wave, and coverage fields

conditional: individual screen functional contract only when reconciliation fails

stage.owner_review_surface: Rendered atlas counts and material product-completeness exceptions only.
next_preflight: entry, terminal, failure, and recovery semantics are known

entries.reason: live stage ledger and validated transition topology

visual_authority.screen_acceptance_scope: Visual-language and platform-baseline authority only; never exact target-screen composition, product semantics, fixture truth, legend-threshold truth, production implementation, or novel-screen fidelity.
visual_authority.visual_language_scope: Linear Graphite shell character, calm professional density, compact contextual navigation, bounded analytical surfaces, concise KPI and command language, visible Result Trust, Focus/Explore character, readable analytical labels and tables, and adaptive external series-panel behavior as a visual-language reference.
visual_authority.reusable_foundation_scope: Hash-pinned source-backed colors, typography stack, spacing rhythm, compact controls, rounded command language, shell/navigation relationships, overlay behavior, and analytical presentation primitives only; exact composition, information architecture, component implementation, runtime semantics, and target-screen acceptance remain later-gate work.

conditional_triggers: individual screen functional contract only when reconciliation fails
